pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/itemFixCopy.ts:17 A two-field Pick is cast to the full StepSpec, and a checked alternative costs almost nothing: genericFixCopy.ts already narrows its other parameter with a Pick (`GradedGate`, line 57), so narrowing `spec` the same way would remove the hatch. Line 64 casts `base as AcceptanceResult` with no stated invariant at all, even though `tier` is optional on Acceptance and required on AcceptanceResult.

techniques.evidence: src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/itemFixCopy.ts:17 The doc comment at lines 8-9 does state the invariant (only archetype and label are read). But the standard's 'when not to use it' rule applies: a verified Pick<StepSpec,'archetype'|'label'> parameter is cheap and the same pattern is already used one parameter over. The sibling cast at line 64 carries no invariant.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/genHistory.ts:157 The history model is a pure transition core. Time arrives as a parameter (`at`), and the hook does the store I/O.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/hash.ts:6 One FNV hash is shared by the generic and Items generators, so they cannot drift apart.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/CliProduce.tsx:33 The prompt logic is a callback seam that about 33 real call sites substitute at, while the panel owns dispatch, retry and live mode.

src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/CliProduce.tsx:62 A mode flag lets a caller switch off the async rejection surfacing, which the doc calls 'the real Rule 4 enforcement path' - the decision the module exists to make. Only the test file uses it.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/genHistory.ts:125 Single-output transforms are written as pipelines. nextSeq is a small loop tracking a running max, which is fine.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/useDispatchPlan.ts:27 The async fetch is confined to an edge hook gated on `enabled`. describeDispatchPlan and genHistory stay synchronous.
src/components/layout-lab/steps/shared/genHistory.ts:108 Inputs are plain records that a test can construct, so no host-minted type needs mirroring.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/index.tsx:81 The store returns CatalogEntityBase[], and all 5 callers repo-wide each cast it to their own entry type with no invariant. Entries carry a literal `catalogId` discriminant, so a typed catalogId-to-entry overload at the store would close every hatch at once.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/index.tsx:81 There is no invariant comment, and the 5/5 call sites each opening their own hatch is the standard's growth signal: the checked surface (catalogStore.ts:212) cannot express what callers need.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/playtime/PlaytimeEstimator.tsx:4 A pure re-export pass-through kept only because of a length metric. The standard says 'Extracting for length is a metric, not a reason'.
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/playtime/playtime-target.ts:4 The budget and lever logic is pure and the components stay thin.
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/playtime/playtime-target.ts:5 Pricing goes through one shared cost table (resolveCosts) and is not restated.

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_world/playtime/playtime-target.ts:77 allocateZoneBudgets is a pipeline. suggestLevers (line 108) is explicitly sequential because its branch arms do different work.
